title: Voice Character
primitive: voice variation in service of the tale (different rooms, different breaths)
summary: A told tale can move through different rooms — and your voice can be the door between them. This kit listens for what changes when the teller picks a different voice for a beat: what the hero sounds like, what the sage holds back, what the ogre lets you say. Phase 1.1 voice-character chooser.

questions.prompt: Pick a 30-second moment in your tale and tell it twice — first as yourself, then as a different voice character (Hero, Sage, Sprite, or Ogre). What did the second voice let you say that the first couldn't?
Which moment is the strongest place to swap voices in a told tale?
options: The Hook — set the room before anything happens.
The Turn — the meaning rotates, and a voice shift makes the rotation audible.
questions.rationale: A voice swap at the Turn signals the rotation. Swapping every line dilutes the shift; swapping only at the Hook locks the room but doesn't move it.

questions.prompt: Listen back to a tale you've already saved with a different voice character applied to one beat. Was the listener's experience louder, quieter, or different in shape?
Take the villain's line in any tale you've told and rewrite it for the Sage. Keep the meaning; change the room. Then read both aloud.

castCameos.line: Voice changes ARE pivots — when the room shifts, the rotation lands.
I lean forward when the voice changes — even before I know what's coming.
A new voice asks the listener to slow. Use it sparingly so the slow still counts.
Picking ONE voice and returning to it through the tale gives the listener a home to leave and come back to.
